style_when: the story is a product, a device, a price or a market for a thing the reader could buy — an appliance, a panel, a router, a robot arm
prompt: Studio product photograph on a home workbench of warm oak: a tall, slightly leaning column of unbranded PLA filament spools wound with cream filament stands on the right third of the frame, and two long unbranded DDR5 memory modules in matte black heat spreaders with gold edge-contact fingers rest across the top, the tiny kit outweighing the whole tower beneath it. Single softbox key light from the left with visible falloff, long cast contact shadows raking across the timber; palette of graphite, bone white and amber; three-quarter angle, 50mm lens, shallow depth of field, fine film grain, generous empty bench to the left, no people, no text, no logos.
negative_prompt: garbled text, random lettering, watermarks, logos
rationale: The story is a straight price comparison between two purchasable goods, which is exactly what a studio product photograph exists for. Staging the tiny RAM kit atop a whole column of spools makes the 22-spool arithmetic visible in one physical paradox, with no numbers on screen. It also rotates the desk away from the recent cinematic, architectural and document treatments.
subject: Two unbranded DDR5 memory modules resting atop a tall stack of PLA filament spools
core_thesis: In one 30-day window the tinkerer's plastic got cheaper while his machine's memory went vertical, so the hobby's real bill moved from what he prints to what the machine remembers.
core_conflict: DDR5 memory repricing into scarcity (a 32GB kit at $474 against a $72 record low, cleared by scalpers and bots) versus a falling PLA consumables market (€18.06/kg, down 11.7% in 30 days), forcing the two-bench tinkerer to choose which purchase to defer.
composition: Extreme asymmetry: the spool column crowned by the RAM kit commands the right third, with long cast shadows and generous empty bench filling the left as negative space.
